architecture.mechanism: Machine learning-based anomaly detection using real-time OBD-II sensor data to identify emission control faults before they cause component damage.
architecture.intervention: Deploy a supervised machine learning diagnostic routine via the dealership OBD-II interface that analyzes engine load, throttle position, and oxygen sensor streams to isolate the root-cause misfire triggering the flashing check engine light, replacing the failed catalytic converter under warranty with verified correction of the upstream fault.
architecture.expected_effect: The upstream misfire condition causing catalyst overheating is identified and repaired, the replacement catalytic converter operates within specification, the flashing check engine light ceases, drivability is restored, and the repair is validated for warranty coverage.
architecture.falsification_test: Log OBD-II PID data during a 50-mile drive cycle after intervention; if the misfire counter increments or the MIL commands a flash state, the mechanism has failed to resolve the root cause.

challenge.kill_reason: the mechanism-space distinctness adjudication counts 0 materially distinct mechanism(s) (< 2, mechanism_distinctness/2.0.0) — the run generated nothing worth attacking (Art. LXXXIV, R514)
